title: fix(cli): os knowledge rebuild and status give the right answer behind a load balancer
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg3zXREECfPtgrM8TPQaxn1v)_

Fixes #37466

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：多节点部署的运维用命令行重建知识源时，进度查询打到别的节点不再直接报失败，而是在共享存储上改看各节点一致的索引状态，并新增一个等待上限选项；查看状态时会说明应答节点上没有构建记录。
- 为什么做：知识库重建运维入口的后续修复，替多节点部署的运维和自动化脚本解决“构建在跑或已成功却被报失败”的问题。
- 出错会怎样：只影响命令行的结论，不影响服务端构建本身；可直接撤回本改动恢复旧行为。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

Design: the card's second option. The build record stays per node (no service change); the CLI falls back to the index state the store reports, which is the same on every node when the adapter's store is shared between nodes (not `memory`).

- `os knowledge rebuild` reads `index_status` once before it starts the build, as the baseline (its index state and its adapter). A progress read answered by a node without this build's record (no record, or a record with another `startedAt`) is no longer an exit 1. It reads the index state instead: when the baseline said a build was due (`due: true`: never built, new fingerprint, changed recipe, no recipe hash on an adapter with `completeBuild`), the index turning `current` means a complete build recorded itself (adapters record the recipe hash only in `completeBuild`), and the command exits 0, saying the counts were not read.
- When no build was due (the index already `current`, `unreadable` from a transient adapter error, or a state that never turns `current`), or the baseline was not read, the index state cannot tell a running build from a finished one (a same-fingerprint rebuild opens no `building` generation in either adapter: `knowledge-memory` and `knowledge-pgvector` `beginBuild`), so the command keeps polling until a read reaches the building node, whose record decides.
- On the `memory` adapter (id `memory`), whose index is a per-process map, the index state is never read as the build's end: each node answers for its own index, so only the building node's record decides. The docs and the status line say the index state is the same on every node only when the adapter's store is shared.
- Failure is reported only on the build's own recorded failure (`failed` / `not-run`) or after the new `--timeout` (seconds, default 600, counted as polls times `--interval`) of reads that reach no record of this build and do not see the index turn `current`. The timeout message says the build may still be running and points at `os knowledge status`; a read that reaches the record starts the timeout again, so a single-node build is never cut off.
- `os knowledge status` labels the record as the answering node's, and when that node holds none says a build run on another node (or before a restart) is not shown, while the index state is the store's.
- `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx` Knowledge section and a patch changeset.

Measured before designing: `index_status` already returns `index` (state, due, detail, held) from the store and `build` (or `null`) from the answering node, so "no record on this node" (`build: null`) and "never built" (`index.state: nothing`) are separate fields; no service change was needed.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts`, new `describe` "a poll that lands on a node without the build record": still running (polls alternate between a node without the record and the building node, exit 0), succeeded (index turns `current`, exit 0), an older record on the answering node read as no record, an index already `current` waits for the building node and reports its recorded failure, an `unreadable` baseline followed by a `current` index elsewhere is no exit 0, the `memory` adapter's `current` index elsewhere is no exit 0 and the building node's record decides, `--timeout` exits 1 with its statement, and the timeout restarts on a read of the record. Existing rebuild tests gained the baseline read.

<details><summary>Readings at 3b351697d</summary>

- `vitest run src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts`: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 14 passed (lock VERDICT command-exit 0).
- Ablation at 91e9a5755 (rebuild.ts restored to the base c385d3bd1, tests kept): Tests 9 failed, 3 passed; restored, green.
- Ablation of the due predicate (put back to the state-based baseline on disk): Tests 1 failed (the unreadable-baseline case), 13 passed; restored.
- Ablation of the memory check (forced false on disk): Tests 1 failed (the memory case), 13 passed; restored.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: VERDICT command-exit 0 (incl. check:test-typecheck OK).

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The `index_status` answer carries no node identity, so `os knowledge status` can only say "the node that answered", never which node ran a build.
- A failed build seen only through other nodes leaves the index due; the CLI cannot read that failure from the store and ends on `--timeout`.
- The memory check matches the adapter id `memory`, the `knowledge-memory` default; a memory adapter registered under another id is not recognised, so for it the index-current exit stays possible.
- `--timeout` counts reads times `--interval`, not wall-clock time; a hung request is not bounded by it (accepted N1).

## Verification

Read first: `packages/cli/src/commands/knowledge/rebuild.ts` (the fallback branch after the record check), then the new tests.
Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/commands/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts` shows 14 passed.
